note: Topical (GSK2981278) and oral (VTP-43742/AGN-242428, BI 730357) RORγt inverse agonists; none passed Phase 2.
label: Psoriasis (RORγt)

engagement.model: Human ex vivo skin (sRICA) and lesional psoriatic skin explants, GSK2981278
engagement.note: Topical GSK2981278 penetrated human skin explants and cut Th17 cytokines; confirmed in lesional psoriatic skin ex vivo.
engagement.short: Ointment cut IL-17 in human skin explants
engagement.quote: Finally, target engagement by this small molecule was confirmed in ex vivo lesional psoriatic skin.
engagement.judgement: Model is the human skin explant assay GSK built to show topical delivery and target engagement before the clinic.

engagement.magnitude_basis: IL-17-pathway transcripts in 4%-treated vs vehicle plaque biopsies
engagement.confidence_note: SID 2017 abstract 249 (J Invest Dermatol 137(5 Suppl)); the journal page returned 403, so the quote is the abstract text as indexed by web search, not read on the page. The same trial (NCT02548052, 15 patients) is Kang 2018 Br J Dermatol 178:1427 (doi:10.1111/bjd.16131, PMID 29150844), paywalled; no registry results posted.
engagement.model: Human ex vivo skin (sRICA) and lesional psoriatic skin explants, GSK2981278
engagement.note: In the plaque test, biopsies of 4%-treated plaques showed no meaningful change in IL-17 biomarkers or the psoriasis signature. A retrodiction (explants public after the 2015 VTP-43742 human IL-17 result) that failed to reproduce it, so contra.
engagement.short: No IL-17 biomarker change in treated plaques
engagement.quote: No meaningful changes in IL-17 related biomarkers or psoriasis disease signature were detected.
engagement.judgement: Explant assay predicted the ointment would reach and suppress IL-17 in skin; patient biopsies did not move. Readout tier proximal: IL-17 transcripts are RORγt's own transcriptional product. Paired by me (abstract does not cite Smith 2016).

engagement.magnitude_basis: ex vivo whole-blood IL-17 inhibition vs the assay IC90
engagement.confidence_note: Year from the Vitae press release 18 Nov 2015 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2015/11/18/788542/31491/en/vitae-pharmaceuticals-announces-positive-top-line-results-from-a-phase-1-multiple-ascending-dose-trial-of-vtp-43742.html): dosed volunteers' blood showed >90% IL-17A suppression over 24 h. Protocol amendment dated 21-Dec-2017, public only with the registry results posting (2021-04-06); dose redacted (350 mg per the protocol text). The 16 Mar 2016 Vitae press release (tier 5) also reported plasma IL-17A/F down up to 75% in patients.
engagement.model: Human whole-blood ex vivo IL-17 secretion assay (IC90 target), VTP-43742/AGN-242428
engagement.note: The sponsor's whole-blood IL-17 IC90 was reached and inhibition held over 24 h in dosed volunteers and patients. First public in Vitae's Nov 2015 healthy-volunteer release; the protocol (posted 2021) states the IC90 target.
engagement.quote: provided a plasma exposure that was ≥ IC90 for inhibition of IL-17 secretion in an ex vivo whole blood assay of IL-17 secretion, and this inhibition was sustained over a full 24 hours duration with chronic dosing.
engagement.judgement: Different model from the 2017 failure (blood ex vivo assay, not topical skin explant), so model_change. AGN-242428 is VTP-43742 under Allergan (protocol: 'formerly Vitae Pharmaceuticals compound VTP-43742'); coded VTP-43742, the name under which the human data were generated.

dose.model: Human ex vivo skin (sRICA) and lesional psoriatic skin explants, GSK2981278
dose.note: Explants set the ointment strengths (0.001–4%); no skin drug level was measured in patients, so the exposure target was never checked.
dose.short: Ointment strengths set on skin explants
dose.quote: Skin biopsy sections were first exposed to GSK2981278 in a simple ointment at approximately half-log increments between 0.001% and 4% strengths.
dose.judgement: The GSK plaque test and NCT03004846 measured plasma, not skin, exposure; whether the topical target was reached is unknown, so GSK2981278 adds no dose comparison.

dose.magnitude_basis: plasma exposure vs whole-blood IL-17 IC90
dose.confidence_note: Year from the Vitae press release 18 Nov 2015 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2015/11/18/788542/31491/en/vitae-pharmaceuticals-announces-positive-top-line-results-from-a-phase-1-multiple-ascending-dose-trial-of-vtp-43742.html) (healthy-volunteer exposure reached the whole-blood target in all but the lowest cohort). Dose values redacted in the posted protocol; 350 mg (IC90) and 700 mg (transaminases) from the protocol text and the 2016 press release.
dose.model: Human whole-blood ex vivo IL-17 secretion assay (IC90 target), VTP-43742/AGN-242428
dose.note: The IC90-based dose was reached without liver signal over 28 days and PASI improved; 700 mg raised transaminases. The exposure half was first public in Vitae's Nov 2015 healthy-volunteer release.
dose.quote: The dose provided a plasma exposure that was ≥ IC90 for inhibition of IL-17 secretion in an ex vivo whole blood assay of IL-17 secretion
dose.judgement: No nonclinical tolerability margin is public, so decision 16 margin_stated is false. BI 730357 is consistent and adds no status change: Ooi 2023 (doi:10.1002/psp4.12948) puts the PASI plateau above 2000 nmol/L against a 140 nM whole-blood IC50 (Harcken 2021).

efficacy.note: 1% GSK2981278 ointment cut epidermal thickening 23% and Th17 cytokines in imiquimod-treated mice.
efficacy.quote: Mice exposed to GSK2981278 exhibited reduced skin redness and scaling, as well as decreased hyperplasia, as evidenced by a 23% reduction in epidermal thickness when compared to the placebo + IMQ-treated group
efficacy.judgement: GSK paired the mouse with the human skin explant; the mouse carries the efficacy prediction.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: AUC change in sonographic infiltrate thickness vs vehicle
efficacy.confidence_note: SID 2017 abstract 249 (J Invest Dermatol 137(5 Suppl)); the journal page returned 403, so the quote is the abstract text as indexed by web search, not read on the page. The same trial (NCT02548052, 15 patients) is Kang 2018 Br J Dermatol 178:1427 (doi:10.1111/bjd.16131, PMID 29150844), paywalled; no registry results posted.
efficacy.note: In the psoriasis plaque test no strength (0.03–4%) thinned the infiltrate, while betamethasone did.
efficacy.short: No strength beat vehicle in plaque test
efficacy.quote: While the positive control showed the expected reduction in infiltrate thickness, there was no reduction in infiltrate thickness with any strength of GSK2981278.

patient_trials.quote: Mean Percent Change From Baseline in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) Score: Part A

efficacy.judgement: Scored as efficacy contra rather than a dose failure: the model package (Smith 2016) explicitly claimed topical delivery into human skin, so the miss belongs to the model. NCT03004846 open-label 4% ointment: PASI +4.3% at day 57 (n=8); Part B never enrolled.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse skin IL-17A mRNA inhibition up to 109% and S100a8/9 up to 95% vs PASI75 30% (Imax 0.56 in Ooi 2023)
efficacy.confidence_note: Year from the NCT03635099 results posting (2022-06-02); abstract-level reading of Gooderham 2025. model_first_use_year 2021 is the mouse data's first public date (proxy; internal use likely earlier).
efficacy.note: Co-primary design: PASI75 30% (200 mg) vs 0% placebo and sPGA 0/1 27.5% vs 0%, both met. Retrodiction: mouse data public 2021, after VTP-43742's 2016 positive Phase 2a; it reproduced it.
efficacy.quote: In part 1, 12 (30.0%) patients achieved PASI75 (P = .0062), and 11 (27.5%) achieved static Physician's Global Assessment of 0/1 (P = .0095) with BI 730357 200 mg versus none receiving placebo.

patient_trials.quote: patients in the 350 mg dose group achieving a 24 percent reduction in the Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI) score relative to placebo.
No data was collected for this Outcome Measure because the study was terminated and no participants reached the Week 16 timepoint.

efficacy.judgement: Direction matched, so same; the mouse's near-total IL-17 suppression over-promised a biologic-like effect (source_calls_it partial). VTP-43742 2016 Phase 2a (press release only, no published model side) and the terminated AGN-242428 trial are listed in patient_trials. Ruling 2026-11-09: efficacy retrodiction counts any drug's earlier patient result for the target; the minicircle data (Harcken, epub 2021-01-05) post-date VTP-43742's March 2016 PASI result, so retro.

safety.confidence_note: No member has an FDA/EMA review; none is in the source bundle.
safety.note: Tox data sit in unpublished IBs; VTP-43742 raised transaminases at 700 mg and AGN-242428's Phase 2 stopped for safety, with no public model prediction to compare.
safety.short: Liver signal; no public tox to compare
safety.quote: Summaries and detailed results of individual studies and assays included in the nonclinical investigational program are included in the investigator's brochure (IB).
safety.judgement: Thymic lymphoma in RORγ-null mice is the known on-target concern but no trial was long enough to test it; the liver signal cannot be scored without the sponsor's tox findings.
